plan.chapterName: OpenStax Precalculus 2e, chapter 8: Further Applications of Trigonometry
plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single sketch on an unlabeled coordinate plane showing a position vector broken into its horizontal and vertical parts. Two thin axes with arrowheads at all four ends meet at the origin; neither axis carries a name or numbers, though a few short tick marks are spaced along them. An orange arrow runs from the origin up and to the right into the first quadrant and is labeled v = ai + bj, with v, i, and j set in bold. A dark blue arrow extends from the origin along the horizontal axis to the point lying directly beneath the orange arrow's tip and is labeled ai below the axis. A second dark blue arrow rises vertically from that point to the tip of the orange arrow and is labeled bj. The two blue arrows and the orange one enclose a right triangle whose legs are the components and whose hypotenuse is the vector. Drawing the components as arrows joined head to tail makes the vector read as their sum rather than as an abstract pair. The sketch supports the magnitude of v being sqrt(a^2 + b^2), read straight off the legs of the triangle.

interactionPlan.concept: A vector v = ai + bj is the head-to-tail sum of its horizontal and vertical component vectors, and its magnitude comes from the right triangle with legs a and b.

interactions.label: Horizontal component a
interactions.teaches: The coefficient a controls the signed horizontal part of ai + bj, so changing a moves the vector endpoint left or right while keeping the vertical contribution separate

interactions.label: Vertical component b
interactions.teaches: The coefficient b controls the signed vertical part of ai + bj, so changing b moves the vector endpoint up or down while preserving the same head-to-tail component structure

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: The component-arrow picture and the right-triangle picture are the same geometry: the vector is the hypotenuse, so its length follows from a^2 + b^2

demo_steps.title: Build the vector from components
demo_steps.narration: The dark blue ai arrow gives the horizontal displacement first, and the dark blue bj arrow then adds the vertical displacement. The orange vector reaches the same final point in one step, so v = ai + bj.

demo_steps.title: Change the horizontal part
demo_steps.narration: Move a to see only the horizontal leg stretch or reverse direction. The vertical leg still begins at the end of the horizontal leg, so the endpoint of v shifts left or right.

demo_steps.title: Change the vertical part
demo_steps.narration: Move b to see only the vertical leg stretch or reverse direction. The vector endpoint moves up or down because bj supplies the signed vertical displacement.

demo_steps.title: Read the magnitude from the triangle
demo_steps.narration: Switch to the magnitude view: the two components are perpendicular legs of a right triangle and the vector is the hypotenuse. Therefore the length of v is sqrt(a^2 + b^2).

interactionPlan.keyInsight: The expression ai + bj is not just notation: it is a horizontal arrow plus a vertical arrow, and together they form the right triangle whose hypotenuse is the vector v.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Use a clean white background with thin black coordinate axes crossing at the origin and arrowheads on all four ends; do not label the axes or number the tick marks. Draw the resultant vector in orange from the origin to (a,b). Draw the component arrows in dark blue: horizontal from the origin to (a,0), then vertical from (a,0) to (a,b). In Components view, emphasize the labels v = ai + bj, ai, and bj, matching the textbook layout with the vector in the first quadrant by default. In Magnitude triangle view, keep the same geometry but replace or supplement component labels with side lengths a, b, |v|, a right-angle marker at (a,0), and the formula |v| = sqrt(a^2 + b^2). If a or b becomes negative, keep arrows signed and place labels near the corresponding leg without overlapping the axes.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for a: the learner changes the horizontal component, the ai arrow length and the endpoint of v move left or right, and the horizontal part of ai + bj is separated from the vertical part.
- Slider for b: the learner changes the vertical component, the bj arrow height and the endpoint of v move up or down, and the vertical part of the vector sum becomes visible.
- Toggle between components and magnitude triangle: the learner switches from labeled component arrows to a right-triangle view with side lengths and sqrt(a^2 + b^2), showing why the vector magnitude follows the Pythagorean theorem.
